editorial:
Ever felt like you were working hard but getting nowhere? That is exactly where you find Fery Kaltenböck. He is a painter in Vienna who thinks he is a genius, but the art world just does not care about him. He is miserable and stuck in a deep rut, so he comes up with a wild plan to get famous. He finds another painter named Blasius Okopenko and decides to turn him into a superstar. The goal is to build him up just to tear him down in a huge public scandal, which Fery thinks will make him the center of attention. It is a mean-spirited game that shows how far some people will go for a little bit of fame.

What really works here is how the power dynamic shifts between the two men. You start off thinking Fery is the one in control, but the twist is that he completely misreads Okopenko. The acting is solid, and it keeps you guessing if the plan will actually work. It is a bit of a slow burn, but it hits hard at the end. If you enjoy stories about ego and betrayal, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Fery's plan backfires completely. He realizes that instead of controlling Okopenko, he has actually become the one being played. The guilt of his actions and the shock of failing so badly push him into a dark place. Unable to handle the shame and his own depression, Fery decides he cannot go on. He ends his own life by hanging himself, proving that his quest for fame destroyed him instead.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological dramas and stories about obsession.
